service_boundary: Represents hosted APIs invoked from NVIDIA's API Catalog, not self-hosted NIM containers, NVIDIA hardware, downloadable model artifacts, or cloud partners operating their own NIM endpoints.
regional_controls: The hosted catalog documentation does not present customer-selected inference regions; production residency controls differ for self-hosted and partner-hosted NIM deployments.
retention_controls: Hosted API use follows NVIDIA API trial and service terms; model-specific and preview conditions must be reviewed before production use.
routing: Customers invoke a selected hosted NIM endpoint; the catalog is not a general automatic multi-provider router.
customization: Portable NIM microservices can be deployed elsewhere, but that customer- or partner-hosted path is outside this hosted-service record.
strengths: A broad multimodal catalog exposes documented APIs backed by NVIDIA's inference stack.
The same NIM packaging concept supports later migration to controlled deployments.
tradeoffs: Catalog-hosted endpoints and self-hosted NIM are materially different service boundaries.
Hosted catalog access may be evaluation-oriented or subject to model-specific availability.
